title: Italian A1 — Foundations
shortDescription: Start from zero and speak everyday Italian for life and work in Italy. Aligned with the CILS A1 Integrazione exam.
description:
A complete beginner course for people who are moving to, or already living in, Italy. In 10 weekly units you learn the Italian you need every day: greeting people, giving your personal details at the Questura or the Comune, talking about your family and your job, renting a flat, shopping, getting around town and visiting the doctor.

Every unit follows the same rhythm: learn new words with pictures and audio, listen to a real-life dialogue, understand one grammar point, then check yourself with a review and a printable study sheet. Each week ends with a live speaking class with a teacher.
objectives:
Introduce yourself and talk about your family, job and home
Fill in forms and handle everyday offices: Questura, Comune, bank, post office
Order at a bar or restaurant, shop at the market and pay
Ask for directions and use public transport
Explain a health problem to a doctor or pharmacist
Prepare for the CILS A1 Integrazione exam

lessons.title: I am, you are: the verb "essere"
lessons.summary: The most important verb in Italian, and when to use "tu" or "Lei".

blocks.title: Il verbo essere
blocks.body:
**Essere** means *to be*. Italians usually drop the subject word (io, tu…) because the verb already shows who is speaking: *Sono indiano* = I am Indian.

- **tu** = you, for friends, family and children
- **Lei** = you, formal: in offices, with doctors, employers and strangers

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **Sono** means both *I am* and *they are*. The rest of the sentence tells you which one.

lessons.title: Numbers to 100 and the verb "avere"
lessons.titleIt: I numeri fino a 100 e il verbo avere
lessons.summary: Big numbers, and the verb you use to say your age.

blocks.title: I numeri fino a 100 e il verbo avere
blocks.body:
**11–19:** undici, dodici, tredici, quattordici, quindici, sedici, diciassette, diciotto, diciannove.

**Tens:** 20 venti, 30 trenta, 40 quaranta, 50 cinquanta, 60 sessanta, 70 settanta, 80 ottanta, 90 novanta, 100 cento.

**Join them together:** venti + tre = **ventitré**. Before *uno* and *otto* the last vowel drops: **ventuno** (21), **ventotto** (28).

To say your age, Italians use **avere** (to have): *Ho 25 anni* = literally "I have 25 years". The **h** is never pronounced.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **ho, hai, ha, hanno** are written with h but sound exactly like **o, ai, a, anno**.

lessons.title: Countries and nationalities
lessons.summary: indiano or indiana? How nationality words change.

blocks.title: Paesi e nazionalità
blocks.body:
Nationality words change for men and women. Most end in **-o** for a man and **-a** for a woman. Words ending in **-e** are the same for both.

To say where you come from:
- **Sono** + nationality: *Sono pakistano.*
- **Sono di** + city: *Sono di Karachi.*
- **Vengo da** + country: *Vengo dall'India, dal Pakistan, dal Bangladesh, dallo Sri Lanka.*

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Nationalities are written with a **small letter** in Italian: *indiano*, not *Indiano*. Countries have a capital: *India*.

lessons.title: My, your: possessives and "the"
lessons.summary: il, la, l' and mio, mia, miei, mie.

blocks.title: Il mio, la mia
blocks.body:
Every Italian noun is **masculine** or **feminine**, and the word for *the* changes:
- **il** (masculine): *il padre* · **la** (feminine): *la madre*
- **l'** before a vowel: *l'acqua, l'indirizzo*
- **lo** before s + consonant and z: *lo studente, lo zio*
- plural: **i** (il), **gli** (lo, l' masc.), **le** (la)

**Possessives** agree with the thing you have, not with you: a man says *mia moglie*, a woman says *mio marito*.

**Rule:** with ONE family member, no article: *mio padre, tua sorella*. In the plural you need it: *i miei figli, le mie sorelle*.

items.italian: I miei figli vanno a scuola.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **Suo** means *his*, *her* and also formal *your*: *Qual è il suo indirizzo?* (What is your address?) — you will hear it in every office.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "My sister lives in Dhaka"

lessons.homework: Write 5 sentences about your family with mio, mia, i miei, le mie.

lessons.title: A, an and plurals
lessons.summary: un caffè, una pizza, due pizze.

blocks.title: Un, una e il plurale
blocks.body:
**A / an** in Italian:
- **un** — most masculine words: *un caffè, un panino*
- **uno** — masculine before s + consonant or z: *uno studente, uno zucchero*
- **una** — feminine: *una pizza*
- **un'** — feminine before a vowel: *un'aranciata*

**Plurals** change the last letter:
- **-o** becomes **-i**: un panino, due panini
- **-a** becomes **-e**: una pizza, due pizze
- **-e** becomes **-i**: un bicchiere, due bicchieri
- words ending with an accent don't change: un caffè, due caffè

items.italian: Vorrei un panino e una bottiglia d'acqua.
items.english: I'd like a sandwich and a bottle of water.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Order like an Italian: number + thing + **per favore**. *Due cappuccini e un tè, per favore.*

lessons.title: A flat for rent
lessons.summary: Ravi phones a landlord about a flat.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: Ravi sees an ad for a flat and phones the landlord (*il proprietario*).

lines.speaker: Ravi

lessons.title: There is, there are
lessons.summary: Describe a place, and say where things are.

blocks.title: C'è e ci sono
blocks.body:
**C'è** = there is (one thing). **Ci sono** = there are (two or more).
- *In cucina c'è un tavolo.* (In the kitchen there is a table.)
- *In camera ci sono due letti.* (In the bedroom there are two beds.)

Questions are the same words with a question tone: *C'è il wifi?* (Is there wifi?)

**Where is it?** sopra (on), sotto (under), accanto a (next to), davanti a (in front of), dietro (behind), dentro (inside).

items.italian: Ci sono due camere da letto.
Le chiavi sono sopra il tavolo.
items.english: The keys are on the table.

items.italian: Il gatto è sotto il letto.
items.english: The cat is under the bed.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Use **c'è / ci sono** to say that something exists. Use **è / sono** to say where a specific thing is: *Il bagno è a destra.*

lessons.title: What time do you start?
lessons.summary: Salim and his neighbour talk about work and hours.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: Salim meets his new neighbour Marco on the stairs. They talk about their jobs and working hours.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.english: Hi Salim! What do you do for work?

lines.speaker: Salim
lines.italian: Faccio il cuoco in un ristorante in centro. E tu?
lines.english: I'm a cook in a restaurant in the centre. And you?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.italian: Io sono infermiere all'ospedale. A che ora inizi a lavorare?
lines.english: I'm a nurse at the hospital. What time do you start work?

lines.speaker: Salim
lines.italian: Inizio alle undici e finisco alle tre. Poi ricomincio alle sette di sera.
lines.english: I start at eleven and finish at three. Then I start again at seven in the evening.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.english: Do you work on Saturdays too?

lines.speaker: Salim
lines.italian: Sì, lavoro dal martedì alla domenica. Il lunedì è il mio giorno libero.
lines.english: Yes, I work from Tuesday to Sunday. Monday is my day off.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.english: What time is it now?

lines.speaker: Salim
lines.italian: Sono le dieci e mezza. Devo andare, ciao!
lines.english: It's half past ten. I have to go, bye!

blocks.body: Timetables, contracts and shifts use the 24-hour clock: **le 14:00** = *le quattordici*. In conversation people say *le due del pomeriggio*.

lessons.title: Days, months and -are verbs
lessons.summary: lavoro, lavori, lavora… and the days of the week.

blocks.title: Giorni, mesi e verbi in -are
blocks.body:
**Days:** lunedì, martedì, mercoledì, giovedì, venerdì, sabato, domenica.
**Months:** gennaio, febbraio, marzo, aprile, maggio, giugno, luglio, agosto, settembre, ottobre, novembre, dicembre.

Days and months are written with a **small letter**. *Il lunedì* = every Monday; *lunedì* = this Monday.

**Regular verbs ending in -are** (lavorare, abitare, parlare, studiare, iniziare): remove **-are** and add the endings below.

items.english: I work from Monday to Friday.

items.italian: Il mio compleanno è a maggio.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: In August (**agosto**) many Italian businesses close for holidays, especially around **Ferragosto** (15 August).

lessons.homework: Write your week: one sentence for each day (e.g. "Il lunedì lavoro. Il sabato studio l'italiano.").

lessons.title: Excuse me, where is…?
lessons.summary: Amrit asks a lady for directions to the post office.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: Amrit needs to send a parcel to India. He asks a lady in the street for directions.

lines.speaker: Amrit
lines.english: Excuse me, madam, where is the post office?

lines.speaker: Signora
lines.italian: L'ufficio postale? È in piazza Sordello.
lines.english: The post office? It's in Piazza Sordello.

lines.speaker: Amrit
lines.english: Is it far?

lines.speaker: Signora
lines.italian: No, è vicino, a cinque minuti a piedi.
lines.english: No, it's near, five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Signora
lines.italian: Vada dritto fino al semaforo, poi giri a sinistra.
lines.english: Go straight on to the traffic lights, then turn left.

lines.speaker: Amrit
lines.italian: Dritto e poi a sinistra. E dopo?
lines.english: Straight on and then left. And after that?

lines.speaker: Signora
lines.italian: Poi prenda la seconda strada a destra. L'ufficio postale è accanto alla banca.
lines.english: Then take the second street on the right. The post office is next to the bank.

lines.speaker: Amrit
lines.english: Thank you very much, madam!

lines.speaker: Signora
lines.english: You're welcome, don't mention it!

items.english: on the right / on the left

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Directions to a stranger use the formal form: **vada** (go), **giri** (turn), **prenda** (take). Friends say *vai, gira, prendi*.

lessons.title: Getting around: transport and "andare"
lessons.titleIt: I mezzi di trasporto e il verbo andare
lessons.summary: Vado in autobus, vado a piedi, vado a Milano.

blocks.title: I mezzi di trasporto e il verbo andare
blocks.body:
**Andare** (to go) is irregular — learn it by heart.

**How you travel:** **in** + transport: *in autobus, in treno, in macchina, in bici*. But: **a piedi** (on foot).

**Where you go:**
- **a** + town: *Vado a Milano.*
- **in** + country: *Vado in India.*
- **in** + many places: *in banca, in farmacia, in ufficio, in piazza*
- **al / alla** + other places: *al supermercato, alla stazione, all'ospedale*

items.english: I go to work by bus.
We're going to Rome by train.

items.italian: I bambini vanno a scuola a piedi.

items.english: Tomorrow I'm going to the bank.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Buy bus tickets at the **tabaccheria** (sign with a big **T**), at the machine or in the app — and **validate** them (*timbrare*) when you get on. Fines are high!

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: It's Saturday morning. Shirin is at the street market (*il mercato*) in the town square.

lessons.title: Colours, clothes and adjectives
lessons.summary: una maglietta rossa, i pantaloni neri.

blocks.title: Colori, vestiti e aggettivi
blocks.body:
In Italian the adjective usually comes **after** the noun and **agrees** with it:
- *una maglietta rossa* (fem.), *un cappello rosso* (masc.)
- *le scarpe rosse*, *i pantaloni rossi*

Adjectives ending in **-e** have only two forms: *verde* / *verdi*.
Some colours never change: **blu, rosa, viola**.

In a clothes shop: *Che taglia porta?* (What size do you wear?) · *Posso provare?* (Can I try it on?) · *Dov'è il camerino?* (Where is the fitting room?)

items.english: What size do you wear? – Medium.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Sales (**i saldi**) happen twice a year: in January and in July. Prices are cut by 30–70%!

lessons.title: At the doctor's
lessons.summary: Bilal has the flu and needs a sick note for work.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: Bilal feels ill and visits his family doctor (*il medico di base*). He also needs a sick note (*il certificato*) for his employer.

lines.speaker: Medico
lines.italian: Buongiorno, si accomodi. Che cosa si sente?
lines.english: Good morning, have a seat. What's wrong?

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.italian: Buongiorno, dottore. Ho mal di testa e mal di gola.
lines.english: Good morning, doctor. I have a headache and a sore throat.

lines.speaker: Medico
lines.english: For how long?

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.italian: Da tre giorni. Ho anche la febbre.
lines.english: For three days. I also have a temperature.

lines.speaker: Medico
lines.english: Do you have your health card?

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.english: Yes, here it is.

lines.speaker: Medico
lines.italian: È un'influenza. Prenda questo sciroppo tre volte al giorno e stia a casa per due giorni.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: In an emergency call **112** (the single European emergency number). For a sick note, your family doctor sends it online to INPS — just ask for **il numero del certificato** to give your employer.

lessons.title: Saying what hurts
lessons.titleIt: Ho mal di… / Mi fa male…
lessons.summary: Two ways to explain pain, plus the pharmacy.

blocks.title: Ho mal di… / Mi fa male…
blocks.body:
**Ho mal di** + body part (no article): *ho mal di testa, mal di denti, mal di schiena, mal di pancia*.

**Mi fa male** + one thing / **Mi fanno male** + more things (with the article):
- *Mi fa male il braccio.* (My arm hurts.)
- *Mi fanno male i piedi.* (My feet hurt.)

Other useful phrases: *Ho la febbre* (I have a fever) · *Ho la tosse* (I have a cough) · *Ho il raffreddore* (I have a cold) · *Sono allergico/a a…* (I'm allergic to…)

items.italian: Ho mal di schiena da una settimana.
items.english: I've had backache for a week.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Pharmacists in Italy are very helpful: for small problems (a cold, a headache) ask them first — *Ho mal di gola, cosa mi consiglia?* (I have a sore throat, what do you recommend?)
